Nora Patel: Hey team — during a tenant migration we noticed ~3k objects that had TTLs in the past week but are still returning in search and GET. Ticket #INC-6221. Example object id: obj_9f3a7c.
Nora Patel: We expect them to be tombstoned/deleted after TTL. API returns 200 on GET and metadata shows "deleted": false. No errors in our app logs.
Emily Chen: Sorry to hear that, Nora. Can you share one full curl repro (GET + delete where applicable) and region? Also were any preserve/legal-hold flags applied?
Nora Patel: Repro below (ap-southeast-1):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/objects/obj_9f3a7c" -i
# response headers include: x-region: ap-southeast-1 x-node: rwd-03
# body: {"id":"obj_9f3a7c","ttl":1678802400,"deleted":false}
```
Nora Patel: We also saw delete webhook attempts (200) but index still shows object present.
Raj Kapoor: Thanks. Quick checks: did the tenant opt into custom retention or a preserve window during migration? Also any recent KMS key rotation?
Nora Patel: No custom retention. We checked UI — default retention of 30 days. KMS rotation happened last month but rotation job reported success.
retention-bot: automated notice: migration-run-2026-03-12 completed; indexer job id idx-774 started.
Leo Martinez: @Raj @Emily please escalate to infra-retention: if KMS/HSM rejects tombstone writes during rotation, storage can keep object alive while index shows tombstone missing. Need KMS audit for delete calls between 1678790000-1678880000.
Emily Chen: Escalating — @infra-retention assigned. Raj, adding repro steps and example object IDs to the ticket.
Raj Kapoor: Repro plan: 1) run GET and record x-node and x-region headers; 2) run DELETE /v1/objects/obj_9f3a7c with ?force=true to see API path; 3) check storage tombstone via admin internal: `GET /admin/objects/obj_9f3a7c/meta` (will return tombstone marker if present). If tombstone missing but delete events were logged, check keystore for KMS errors.
Nora Patel: I ran DELETE and got 202 accepted, no body. After 10m GET still returned deleted:false.
Raj Kapoor: Please paste the raw 202 response headers (x-request-id, x-node). That helps trace the delete through the pipelines.
Nora Patel: x-request-id: rwd-req-99321 x-node: rwd-03
Raj Kapoor: Good — that matches indexer node. Next step: engineering will pull auditlogs for that x-request-id and cross-check HSM/KMS responses. Also will re-run indexer rehydrate job for that node.
Leo Martinez: Also confirm whether any preserve flag was set by data-migration tool. If preserve=true was flipped during migration, objects will be retained regardless of TTL.
Nora Patel: Confirmed migration tool did NOT set preserve.
Emily Chen: ETA: infra team will investigate KMS audit and indexer backlog, will follow up in 4 hours. In the meantime, as a mitigation run: `POST /admin/purge?tenant=TENANT_ID&mode=index-first` — this will reindex and attempt to apply tombstones. Use with caution.
Nora Patel: Ok we will try index-first purge on a small set and report results. Thanks all. :pray:
__notes: This document is a single Slack thread content string with messages in chronological order. No title field included per agents.md.
